summary: Created `helpdesk` on node1 with permission to restart only `sshd.service`. Verified allowed and denied operations, then rebooted node1 and confirmed persistence and recovery under a changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Created the standard `helpdesk` account with no supplemental administrative groups.
Installed a root-owned, mode-0440 sudoers rule allowing only `/usr/bin/systemctl restart sshd.service` without a password.
Verified that `helpdesk` successfully restarts SSH and that SSH remains directly reachable.
Verified that root identity access, restarting another service, and stopping SSH are denied.
Safely rebooted node1 and revalidated the account, sudo policy, SSH health, and restrictions.

evidence.summary: Shows the account, UID/GID, standard-group-only membership, home and shell; confirms persistence after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Allow helpdesk to restart SSH with sudo
evidence.summary: Shows the validated exact-command sudoers rule and successful pre- and post-reboot SSH restarts with changed daemon PIDs and reachable port 22.
Shows no administrative-group membership, only one listed sudo command, and denial of root identity, another-service restart, and SSH stop operations.

Captures healthy pre-reboot state, native reboot acknowledgement, boot-ID change from 738d0aac-71a1-4191-8a37-bf00edfeff5d to a0e68ece-4bda-4999-bfab-42941929bb3e, and recovered account, sudo policy, SSH service, listener, and direct reachability.
